transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-21
Time: 15:00-15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno, Sofia Liang (Redwood); Maya Patel, Jon Roper, Leah Kim (Verdantia)

Summary (auto): Renewal/expansion check-in. Discussed required capacity uplift for Q2 ramp, region preferences (EU-West then APAC), options for Dedicated vs Hosted, and next steps for benchmarks and procurement.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya (Verdantia): Hi Alex, Maya here.
[00:08] Jon (Verdantia): Jon here.
[00:10] Leah (Verdantia): Leah on procurement.
[00:12] Sofia (Redwood): Sofia here from solutions engineering.
[00:15] Alex: Cool. We scheduled 50 minutes to run through where you are on renewal and the region stretch. Quick agenda: sizing needs, region order, whether you want Dedicated or Hosted for the uptick, and procurement timeline. Sound good?
[00:30] Maya: Yep, that's perfect. We've got a ton of traffic expected starting May, mostly inference for classification and some reranking. Our estimate is about 30M tokens/day now trending up, want to plan for 3x during the summer.
[00:45] Jon: To add, latency is important for our interactive product — sub-200ms P95 on small prompts. Cost also matters, we can't blow the budget.
[00:55] Sofia: Thanks, that helps. Two quick clarifying questions: are those token numbers for raw model tokens or include embeddings/metadata? And do you have a target for failover in case a region is down?
[01:10] Maya: Tokens are raw generation tokens. Embeddings are separate, but not massive right now. For failover — we need cross-region fallback and a 30-minute RTO ideally.
[01:25] Jon: Also we will want audit logs for every inference call because of regulatory reasons in EU, and keys kept in our KMS for private pilot.
[01:35] Alex: Noted. On region preference — you mentioned EU-West first, then APAC. Is that still the sequence?
[01:42] Maya: Yes EU-West first, we have compliance review in March and want a soft launch in April for EU users. APAC we'll want by June.
[01:51] Sofia: Ok. For EU we have two options: Hosted with EU-only data residency (we can put the serving in eu-west) or Redwood Dedicated with private VPC and customer KMS. Dedicated gives isolation and predictable throughput but is a longer lead time.
[02:10] Leah: Can you ballpark lead times? Procurement wants to know so we can schedule legal review.
[02:16] Alex: Hosted EU-only: usually 2-3 weeks to enable region and route traffic. Dedicated/VPC: provisioning GPUs and setting up network tends to be 6-8 weeks, sometimes longer if on-prem certificates or HSMs are involved.
[02:30] Jon: Hm. 6-8 weeks could be tight for our June APAC plan. Is there a hybrid — start Hosted in EU to hit the April date and then flip to Dedicated after?
[02:40] Sofia: That's exactly what most customers do. Start hosted for speed, then migrate workloads to Dedicated; we support blue-green style rollouts and model pinning so you don't lose traffic during the change.
[02:52] Maya: Good. About capacity, what does Redwood recommend for cost/perf for 3x current traffic? We're seeing spikes that cause cold-start latency.
[03:02] Sofia: Two levers: intelligent batching and KV prefix caching for repeated conversational contexts. Also pick quantized model variants if quality tolerates it. For throughput, Dedicated with autoscale policies gives the best predictable latency and unit cost; hosted can handle bursts but at slightly higher unit cost.
[03:20] Alex: For example, if you commit to a reserved pool of X GPUs for 12 months we can model token/unit economics. I'll send a pricing template after this call.
[03:28] Leah: Great. On the security side, we need SOC2, ISO docs, and KMS integration details for legal. Can you share the SOC2 report and a KMS integration whitepaper?
[03:40] Alex: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2, and Sofia will include the KMS/HSM integration notes.
[03:46] Sofia: Quick technical aside — when you run the benchmark, please include realistic conversation lengths. The KV cache behavior changes cost and latency a lot. We saw that with a medial customer where the prefix cache reduced tokens by ~17%.
[04:00] Jon: Ok we'll provide a prompt set. How do you want the benchmark run — Redwood runs it or we run on our side?
[04:08] Sofia: We can run it both ways. We recommend we run a first pass with our harness to validate latency under expected QPS, then you can run an in-house run for procurement confidence. We'll share the harness and raw data.
[04:20] Alex: Let's put that in the action items.

[04:30] — mid-call deep dive —

[04:30] Sofia: I want to walk through a sample throughput profile. If you expect 3x tokens/day and 20% of requests are low-latency interactive, we'd recommend a split of dedicated baseline for the interactive tier and hosted bursts for batch-like loads.
[04:50] Maya: Split sounds fine. What's the recommended sizing per GPU?
[04:55] Sofia: It depends on model variant. For quantized 8-bit Llama-style models we typically get X tokens/sec on A100-like instances; on lower latency models you lose some throughput. I'll put concrete numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:10] Jon: We use a mix of small and medium models in prod; likely will standardize on one variant for cost reasons. Also, any known issues with KV cache across regions? We want cache warming to avoid first-token spikes.
[05:25] Sofia: KV cache is per-host. For cross-region warm starts we recommend prefix caching in the app layer and a warmup flow when switching regions. We also have automatic fallback and prewarmed instances for Dedicated. There are some nuance with sequence length distribution — longer sequences need more memory and change kernel selection.
[05:46] Maya: Understood. Next, procurement timeline — Leah, anything to flag?
[05:50] Leah: We need a vendor questionnaire answered, standard SOC2 docs, and a sample SLA with credits. Also, the legal team wants to see cancellation and exit terms for Dedicated.
[06:02] Alex: We'll include an exit plan and data deletion commitments. Our typical SLA for Dedicated includes uptime targets and response windows; I can share the redlined sample.
[06:10] Leah: Perfect. Also pricing bands — we may want a step-up option if we cross a usage threshold mid-term.
[06:18] Alex: We can model step-up pricing in the 12-month commitment scenario.

[06:25] — timestamped Q/A and small interruptions —

[06:25] [06:25] Jon: One more technical: do you support VPC peering or do we need a transit? Our infra team prefers explicit peering for audit trails.
[06:34] Sofia: We support VPC peering and customer-managed NAT gateways; for on-prem we support an air-gapped package but that's a longer engagement.
[06:42] Maya: For EU cluster, will we have separate audit logs or aggregated logs across regions?
[06:48] Alex: We can provide token-level logs per region, and also an aggregated view in the Console. For the private pilot we can forward logs to your SIEM via syslog/S3.
[06:58] Maya: Good.

[07:05] — benchmarking logistics —

[07:05] Sofia: For the benchmark we'll need your sample prompt set, QPS target, and a small test account for validation. We'll run a 4-hour soak and a few spike tests.
[07:15] Maya: I'll get the prompt set over by Friday.
[07:18] Alex: Friday is great. We'll aim to have initial benchmark results within 72 hours after we receive it.

[07:25] — pricing scenarios discussion —

[07:25] Alex: Quick walk-through of two pricing scenarios: 12-month commitment with reserved Dedicated capacity vs 6-month flexible commitment with hosted plus burst. The 12-month reserved gives ~25% lower per-token cost at predicted volumes.
[07:40] Leah: Is that net of egress and data transfer costs? We need a full TCO number.
[07:46] Alex: We'll include egress, storage for KV cache snapshots, and any VPC peering charges in the template.

[07:55] — procurement nitty-gritty and compliance —

[07:55] Leah: For KMS we require BYOK (bring your own key) support and key rotation documentation.
[08:03] Sofia: We support BYOK via AWS KMS or external HSM; key rotation is supported and we can provide the integration guide.

[08:12] — discussion about migration strategy —

[08:12] Jon: If we start hosted in EU and then migrate to Dedicated, how do you handle KV cache warm-up and session continuity?
[08:21] Sofia: We can replicate prefix cache metadata and provide a migration tool. Also, we recommend a brief warmup window and sticky routing for sessions during initial migration. That reduces cold-starts.
[08:33] Maya: Nice.

[08:40] — customer constraints and timeline recap —

[08:40] Maya: High-level timeline: procurement sign-off mid-Feb, EU hosted launch in early April, Dedicated/VPC pilot for sensitive workloads May-June, APAC go-live in June.
[08:53] Alex: That aligns with the 6-8 week lead for Dedicated if you sign in February. If procurement slips a week we're still ok by shifting some work in parallel.
[09:02] Leah: We'll aim for Feb 10 procurement approval. I'll confirm internally.

[09:10] — miscellaneous clarifications and small talk —

[09:10] Jon: One more: are there any rate-limiting knobs per token that we should be aware of at the API layer?
[09:17] Sofia: Yes, we expose per-route rate limits, token-based quotas, and burst windows. We can set token budgets per team and per model.
[09:26] Alex: Ok, let's go to wrap-up and agree on next steps.

[09:30] Wrap-up:
[09:30] Alex: Quick recap: 1) Verdantia to confirm region choice and provide prompt set by Friday (Maya). 2) Redwood to run benchmark and share results (Sofia). 3) Alex to send pricing scenarios and SLA template (Alex). 4) Leah to start procurement intake and vendor questionnaire.
[09:48] Maya: Yes — Maya will get the prompt sets and expected QPS.
[09:51] Leah: I'll start procurement and target Feb 10 decision.
[09:55] Alex: Great. Are we comfortable with a follow-up in two weeks to review benchmark results and pricing?
[10:02] Jon: Two weeks works.
[10:04] Sofia: We'll block time.

[10:10] Alex: Anything else?
[10:12] Maya: No, that's it. Thanks.
[10:14] Alex: Thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription: there are a few mishears (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV cash), small overlaps and filler words. Full transcript clipped for length but core QA and action items captured.

End of meeting.
